Leah: Follow-up from today's all-hands infra Q&A: short answers and action items about GPU regions and autoscaling.
Omar: Quick summary: SIN pilot + TOK sibling region. Priority is predictable capacity for Dedicated customers, then Hosted stability.
Rina: We provisioned two reserved pools in SIN and one shared burst pool in KUL for Hosted pilot. Burst uses spot VMs and can be reclaimed.
Leah: If spot is reclaimed mid-request what happens?
Omar: Short: drain window ~20s, snapshot KV cache often; if eviction is abrupt we return 502 and retry to next fallback with trace id.
Rina: Fallback order: local reserved -> local burst -> TOK -> US-west. Console will warn on cross-region fallback and show estimated egress.
Leah: For customers with strict residency, what's the control?
Rina: Route flag `avoid_cross_region_fallback: true`. When set we will not reroute; instead return 429 with `x-rdi-reason: residency-block`. We'll add sample config and error text in the doc.
Leah: Billing concerns?
Omar: We'll show a "burst allowance" in Console and send alerts when burst spend exceeds a threshold. No surprise charges without opt-in for cross-region.
devops-bot: autoscaler v1.2 canary started -> 5% traffic.
Rina: Action items: (1) API schema PR to add the route flag by Thu, (2) Console to add burst opt-in wireframe next sprint, (3) SRE to validate cold-start telemetry in APAC pilot.
Omar: Cold-start targets: node <=90s, model warm-up median ~25s for small variants, up to 75s for largest. We'll pre-warm frequent models.
devops-bot: canary successful. Autoscaler v1.2 deployed to 5%.
Leah: I'll compile PR links and customer comms draft and share in #product-announcements. Thanks everyone.
